summary: Verified httpOnly-cookie auth migration on backend + frontend. Backend pytest (test_iter16_cookie_auth.py) 7/7 PASS: login sets admin_token cookie (HttpOnly=True, Secure=True, SameSite=None); /api/admin/me & /api/admin/stats work with cookie only; POST /api/admin/logout returns 200 and subsequent /api/admin/me returns 401; X-Admin-Token header fallback still authenticates (dual-mode); admin1/chelyn/admin3 all log in; cookie-authenticated regression on /admin/orders,/admin/stats,/admin/users,/admin/logs,/admin/bendahara all 200. localStorage confirmed to store only mbi_admin_user (no token). CRITICAL FRONTEND BUG FOUND: after a page refresh on /admin, /walkin, and /checkin the app shows the login screen again even though the httpOnly cookie is still valid and /api/admin/me returns 200. Root cause: AdminPage.js:1594, WalkinPage.js:97, CheckinPage.js:66 all initialize `const [authed] = useState(!!localStorage.getItem(ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY))`, but the security migration removed the token from localStorage — so `authed` is always false on first render after a refresh, and the Login component is rendered instead of the dashboard. Session breaks on every hard refresh across all staff pages. This exactly matches the scenario the request flagged as a real bug.

ui_bugs.issue: Line 1594: useState(!!localStorage.getItem(ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY)) — token no longer stored in LS after cookie migration, so page refresh always shows login screen even though httpOnly cookie is valid and /api/admin/me returns 200.
Line 97: same pattern — refresh on /walkin returns to login screen despite valid cookie session.
Line 66: same pattern — refresh on /checkin returns to login screen despite valid cookie session.

integration_issues.issue: Cookie flows correctly to backend on refresh (verified /api/admin/me = 200 in the browser context), but the React state gate uses localStorage.getItem(ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY) which is now permanently null. Result: authed=false on every mount, Login component rendered.

action_items: Fix session gating on refresh in AdminPage.js, WalkinPage.js, CheckinPage.js. Suggested minimal fix: replace `useState(!!localStorage.getItem(ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY))` with `useState(!!getAdminUser())` (import getAdminUser from apiClient) since setAdminSession still writes ADMIN_USER_KEY and clearAdminSession removes it. Better fix: on mount, call /api/admin/me and set authed based on 200 vs 401 to make cookie the single source of truth.
Also verify all other places that gate UI on ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY (search entire frontend for `ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY` and `mbi_admin_token`).
After fix, retest hard-refresh on /admin, /walkin, /checkin — user must remain on the dashboard.

On /admin, the 'Keluar' button was not immediately visible at desktop 1920x1080 during automated test (count=0) — likely nested in a menu; confirm logout entry point is discoverable on desktop, not only in a hamburger.
critical_code_review_comments: Security migration is correctly implemented on backend (httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=None, 7d) and cookie/header dual auth works. However the frontend state initializer was not updated to match — this is a coordinated-change miss. The pattern `!!localStorage.getItem(ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY)` appears in at least 3 pages and must be replaced everywhere.
apiClient.setAdminSession still accepts (token,user) but discards `token` — signature should be simplified to setAdminSession(user) to prevent confusion / future reintroduction of the token in LS.

clearAdminSession removes both keys — fine, but consider also calling POST /api/admin/logout from clearAdminSession (or documenting that callers must) so that server-side cookie is always cleared in tandem.

SameSite=None + Secure is required for cross-site cookie flow; since backend and frontend share the preview domain here it works, but on any future subdomain split (e.g. api.kbikepri.com) the CSRF surface widens. Consider SameSite=Lax if same-site is guaranteed post-launch.

CORS_ORIGINS is still '*' with allow_credentials=False in the doc, but cookie auth REQUIRES credentials from the browser. Same-origin here masks the risk; before production behind a separate API domain, set CORS_ORIGINS to explicit list AND allow_credentials=True.
server.py ~1950 lines — recurring comment, still not split into routers.

success_rate.frontend: 60% (login/cookie/logout/backend-visible-to-frontend all OK; hard-refresh session persistence FAILS on all 3 staff pages)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug reproduction: log in at /admin (or /walkin, /checkin), verify dashboard loads, then hit browser refresh (F5) — login screen reappears even though document.cookie shows admin_token=... (httpOnly, so not visible via JS, but request.cookies works — you can confirm via `await page.evaluate(async()=>({s:(await fetch('/api/admin/me',{credentials:'include'})).status}))` → 200. The fix is 3 one-line changes in AdminPage.js/WalkinPage.js/CheckinPage.js swapping the useState initializer. After fix, keep test_iter16_cookie_auth.py green and add a Playwright refresh regression.
rca_of_the_issue: Frontend security migration removed token storage from localStorage (correct) but did not update the 3 staff pages that use `useState(!!localStorage.getItem(ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY))` as the initial authenticated-state gate. On refresh, the initializer runs before any effect, returns false, and the Login component is mounted. The backend cookie is still valid (browser sends it automatically and /api/admin/me returns 200), but the UI never queries it. Mitigation: (a) short-term: replace initializer with `!!getAdminUser()` since user object is still in LS; (b) durable: add a mount-time /api/admin/me probe and set authed from its status, making the cookie the single source of truth.
